=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:9120 | severity=NIT | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: git rev-parse commands inside marker generation are unguarded — `$(git -C "${judge_wt}" rev-parse HEAD)` and `$(git -C "${judge_wt}" rev-parse "refs/remotes/origin/${default_branch}")` run without exit checks. If either fails after the earlier fetch succeeded (race, filesystem error, orphaned worktree), the guidance comment carries `head=` or `base=` empty values, the prepare-side matcher at review_conflict_prepare.sh:481 never finds it, and the function returns 4 without dispatching the resolver.
  WHY: A transient ref-resolution failure silently produces a guidance comment that can never be matched, leaving the integration conflict unresolved. The prior git fetch (line 8920) makes this a narrow race window but not impossible.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6912-6917 | severity=NIT | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `summary="$(jq -r '.summary' "${verdict_file}")"` returns the literal string `null` when the verdict JSON omits the `summary` key, and `security_pass_prose "${summary}"` renders it as-is, so the terminalization comment reads `**Summary:** null`.
  WHY: A verdict produced without a summary key (hand-crafted fixture, sandbox failure partial output) posts a misleading operator-facing comment.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:LAST RUN DIFF lines 6883-6891, `summary="$(jq -r '.summary' "${verdict_file}")"` | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: When the verdict JSON lacks a `summary` field, `jq -r` returns the literal string `null`, which is then passed to `security_pass_prose` and rendered as `**Summary:** null` in the tracking comment.
  WHY: A verdict produced by a sandbox failure, hand-written fixture, or model output that omits the summary field will post a terminalization comment displaying `**Summary:** null` to operators instead of omitting the line or showing a fallback. The `security_pass_prose` function has no guard for this case.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:LAST RUN DIFF lines 6286-6337, `test_security_pass_cap_never_waives_a_high_finding` | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Converting from `@pytest.mark.parametrize("severity", ["high","critical","unknown"])` to a `for severity in (...)` loop reduces test failure isolation.
  WHY: When an assertion fails for an earlier severity (e.g., "high"), pytest stops execution and later severities ("critical", "unknown") never run or get individually reported. A regression specific to one severity surfaces as the same test name rather than a parameterized variant, masking which severity actually failed and whether the others still pass.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- README.md:Line 2346, the "Security backstop" paragraph added in LAST RUN DIFF: "Legacy rows without an exploit scenario suppress by exact ID only." | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The README states legacy waivers without an exploit scenario suppress findings by exact finding ID only. Both enforcement paths (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6253-6256 and scripts/security_audit.sh:1628-1631) also require any populated `severity` and `owasp_or_stride_category` on the waiver to match the finding, even when the finding ID matches exactly. A legacy waiver with no exploit scenario but a populated severity (e.g., "high") will not suppress a same-ID finding whose severity changed.
  WHY: An operator reading this README sentence could expect a legacy waiver to suppress all same-ID findings regardless of severity or category changes. The actual enforcement is stricter than documented, so a re-reported finding with a different severity would not be suppressed, potentially causing unnecessary terminalization. The behavior is safer than documented (more matching, not less), but the documentation is misleading.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:test_security_pass_cap_never_waives_a_high_finding (lines 6292-6313, modified in LAST RUN DIFF) | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The test was converted from `@pytest.mark.parametrize("severity", ["high", "critical", "unknown"])` to a `for severity in ("high", "critical", "unknown")` loop. With parametrize, each severity is a separate test case with its own test ID (`...[high]`, `...[critical]`, `...[unknown]`). With the loop, if the "high" iteration fails an assertion, "critical" and "unknown" never execute, and the failure surfaces as a single `test_security_pass_cap_never_waives_a_high_finding` failure without severity-specific identification.
  WHY: No runtime failure — the test still validates all three severities when passing. This is a test debuggability regression: a failure on one severity masks potential severity-specific regressions in the others and loses the per-severity test ID in CI output.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
